source.note: No real product. A generic Japandi visual proxy made for the demo catalogue; it copies no retailer's design and carries no brand.
source.generation: Higgsfield multi_image_to_3d from a four-view AI turnaround sheet generated with the Codex image_gen tool (codex-image.sh); should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=30000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging and animation off.
source.postProcessing: @gltf-transform/cli resize --width 1024 --height 1024, then scripts/fit_glb.py per-axis fit (centres the footprint, puts the base at y=0).
source.priceProvenance: invented: a plausible demo figure, not a real or quoted price

knownLimitations: No real product. Generic Japandi visual proxy generated from an AI turnaround sheet; the catalogue price is invented, not sourced.

The rug is genuinely flat and was NOT inflated by the generator. Raw mesh height was 1.45 cm against a 190 cm width (0.8%), and in the shipped file 13511 vertices lie on the bottom plane and 13183 on the top plane with only about 1200 on the 2 cm rim: two parallel planes and a thin edge, not a pillow.

Requested 200 x 300 x 2 cm. The generated footprint is squarer than requested (raw 190 x 161 cm, about 1.18:1, against the requested 1:1.5) and its long axis runs along X rather than Z, so scripts/fit_glb.py hit its 10% anisotropy cap: the shipped rug is 258.4 x 241.6 x 2.0 cm. Thickness matches exactly; the footprint is a large near-square area rug, not a 200 x 300 rectangle. fit_glb.py exited 1, outside the repository's asset-check tolerance.

Not inspected in a render; no render was available to this agent. The source turnaround sheet showed four flat rugs at a low three-quarter angle with a visible thin cut edge, oatmeal ground and narrow grey woven stripes.
PBR textures resized to 1024 px, so the herringbone flatweave texture is softer than the source sheet.
